extraction_scope.mechanism_source_type: primary text, molecular-dynamics figures, and supplementary figure docx captions

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports a structure-activity interpretation that replacing E4/A8/S12/A18 in Alyteserin-1c increased charge/hydrophilicity and shifted activity toward Gram-positive targets.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is inferred from peptide design plus MIC/MHC phenotypes; it is not a direct membrane-disruption assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular dynamics models associate peptide helical stability with antimicrobial selectivity in E. coli and S. aureus membrane models.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: WT and ΔM peptides in bacterial membrane models
mechanism_claims.limitations: MD evidence is computational support and is not promoted to direct mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper proposes His20 hydrogen-bond interactions with membrane phospholipids as a contributor to peptide stability/selectivity.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: His20 region of WT and ΔM peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Hydrogen-bond counts come from MD analysis, so the claim remains model-based.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Staphylococcal peptidase I prediction supports a protease-susceptibility distinction: WT has one predicted E4 cleavage site and ΔM has none.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an in silico cleavage prediction, not an observed protease assay.

supplementary_review.conclusion: Supplementary archive contains two DOCX figure files with secondary-structure timeline and membrane-placement captions; no supplementary activity/toxicity table was recovered.
